Exam vocabulary

Translate question wording into architecture

WordingMeaningLikely answer
Must, guarantee, enforceModel discretion is insufficientBackend gate, permission, hook, schema, or explicit invocation
Most token efficientRemove unnecessary model workProject or normalize before context; script mechanical edits
Best immediate fixFollow the stated failure signalmax_tokens means more output capacity or smaller output

Core rule: put each requirement at the lowest layer that can enforce it reliably. Prompts guide; code, permissions, schemas, hooks, and backends enforce.

Claude Code

Clear compact fork and project rules

  • /compact instructions continues the same task with a generated summary. Preserve goals, modified files, decisions, and tests.
  • /clear starts a new conversation with empty context. Files already changed on disk remain unchanged.
  • Branch or fork copies an earlier starting context, so it is not complete isolation.
  • Ephemeral CI container provides reliable runtime isolation between automated jobs.
  • Root CLAUDE.md carries recurring project guidance. A hook plus CI is stronger when literal enforcement is required.
  • Large migration: PLAN → EXECUTE → TEST. Plan mode is a phase, not the finished task.
  • Bulk mechanical change: generate and run a deterministic script, then inspect the diff and tests.
.claude/settings.json
{
  "permissions": {
    "deny": ["Read(./.env.production)", "Read(./.env.*)"]
  }
}

A Read deny rule protects built-in file tools. Add sandbox filesystem restrictions when Bash subprocesses also need OS-level protection.

Tools and controls

Know where enforcement belongs

LayerPurposeExample
Prompt or CLAUDE.mdGuide behaviorPrefer Tailwind; describe escalation cases
Routing classifierProtect expensive contextFilter weather questions before support agent
PreToolUseBlock or ask before executionRefund amount or security policy check
Tool backendEnforce every callerRequire a valid identity session token
PostToolUseValidate or replace completed outputFormat, lint, test, or return updatedToolOutput
CI validatorIndependent evidenceTests, schema validation, policy audit

tool_choice: any forces at least one tool, not a specific tool and not a prerequisite order. It cannot replace an identity gate.

Tool contract: distinctive name, when to use, when not to use, exact inputs, output shape, limits, and neighboring alternatives. Project unused fields and normalize backend formats before the model sees them.

Message Batches API

Batch ID tracks the job custom ID tracks the request

POST /v1/messages/batches
{
  "requests": [{
    "custom_id": "document-0042",
    "params": {
      "model": "<current-model-id>",
      "max_tokens": 1200,
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Extract ..."}]
    }
  }]
}
  1. Assign a unique custom_id that maps to the source record.
  2. Store the returned batch ID and poll overall processing status.
  3. Retrieve results and map every entry by custom_id; result order is not submission order.
  4. Inspect each result type and error. Chunk only context-limit failures.
  5. Resubmit with traceable IDs such as document-0042-part-01.

Boundary: Message Batches improves asynchronous throughput and price. It does not enlarge one request’s context or improve retrieval recall. Use parallel tool calls when the current live response needs several independent results.

Structured output and retrieval

Match the symptom to the repair

  • ISO calendar date: use JSON Schema {"type":"string","format":"date"}.
  • Optional: field may be absent. Nullable: field exists but no confident value is available.
  • Cut-off JSON with stop_reason: max_tokens: increase output capacity or reduce and chunk the requested output.
  • Correct value in the wrong object: error-feedback retry can repair the transformation.
  • Fact absent from the source: retry cannot invent evidence; return null or absent, obtain another source, or escalate.
  • Long-document recall: split into overlapping windows so boundary evidence survives.
  • Rare document types: guarantee a minimum sample per type, then allocate remaining samples by volume or risk.
  • Prompt caching: cache a stable prefix. The write has a premium, later reads are cheaper, and output pricing is unchanged.

Agents and SDKs

Fresh review coordinated flow and current SDK behavior

  • Independent reviewer: fresh context with original task, rubric, final artifact, and necessary evidence. Exclude the researcher’s confidence and persuasive reasoning.
  • Hub and spoke: subagents return results to the coordinator, which owns dependencies and routes evidence.
  • Terminal state: a stopped loop is not necessarily resolved. End as completed, failed, or handoff-ready with a clear owner and preserved state.
  • Client SDK Tool Runner: can automate custom tool calls, tool results, and loop management.
  • Claude Agent SDK: adds the Claude Code runtime and built-in tools such as Read and Bash, plus sessions, hooks, permissions, and subagents.
  • Agent SDK subagent: explicitly naming a configured agent is documented as guaranteed invocation.
  • Interactive Claude Code subagent: natural-language naming influences delegation; an @-mention guarantees the chosen agent for one task.

Course corrections

Do not memorize these outdated answers

.claudeignoreCurrent answer: permissions.deny in .claude/settings.json, plus sandboxing when Bash must also be constrained.

PostToolUse regex for ISO datesCurrent Structured Outputs support JSON Schema format: date. Application validation can still add defense in depth.

Client SDK always needs a handwritten loopOutdated because current Client SDK Tool Runner automates the lifecycle.

Named subagent has one universal ruleAgent SDK and interactive Claude Code use different documented guarantees.

Always use /clear in long sessionsUse /compact to continue the same task; reserve /clear for a new task or polluted context.

Five-minute scan

Final recognition sheet

  1. Guarantee means a programmatic mechanism, not stronger wording.
  2. Compact continues; clear starts a new conversation; neither reverts disk changes.
  3. tool_choice: any means some tool, not the correct tool or order.
  4. PreToolUse runs before; PostToolUse runs after.
  5. Business invariants belong in the backend.
  6. Batch ID tracks the job; custom_id tracks each request.
  7. Batching improves throughput, not context capacity or recall.
  8. High recall needs overlapping chunks and minimum sampling floors.
  9. max_tokens truncation requires more capacity or smaller output.
  10. Retry can fix placement; it cannot create missing evidence.
  11. Cache stable prefixes; output tokens retain normal pricing.
  12. Project and normalize tool output before model context.
  13. Fresh reviewer context reduces anchoring.
  14. Client Tool Runner and Agent SDK are different abstraction levels.
  15. Plan, then execute and test.
